messages:
tess: heads-up - quick canary caused starter sample to fail on node 18. dynamic `import()` ended up loading cjs and threw "Cannot use import statement outside a module".
omar: that usually points at the package exports resolution. can you paste the exports block from the published package?
tess: here (from the unpacked tarball):
```json
"exports": {
  ".": { "import": "./dist/esm/index.js", "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js" },
  "./helpers/*": "./dist/helpers/*.js"
}
```

jen: did the tarball actually include the esm file? sometimes our build step omits it when building only cjs for canaries.
tess: tarball only had cjs. odd thing is node still picked the require branch for a dynamic import.
omar: Node conditional exports can be sensitive to how the object is encoded. our publish tooling (manifest-merge) sorts keys which can flip resolution in some node versions.
jen: ack. short fix: revert the canary, republish ensuring the esm path exists. medium fix: change pack workflow to write exports with a stable/deterministic serializer that preserves conditional order. add a CI unpack+assert that verifies the exported map matches expected. also add a small samples smoke test that does `await import('@redwood/sdk')` on node-18 in CI.
ci-bot: job 712 failed: node-18 dynamic import smoke test failed. logs: https://ci.internal/712
tess: I'll roll back the canary and open the PR for the pack fix + CI check. will update onboarding docs to remind contributors to verify sample imports on LTS nodes.
jen: also worth adding a lint or serializer util so teams don't cobble ad-hoc writes to package.json. saved me debugging time last week.
tess: agreed. thanks all.
